learn: Health-related fitness has five parts: cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility and body composition.
Cardiovascular endurance is how well your heart and lungs work during long activity.
Muscular strength is how much force a muscle can make; muscular endurance is how long it can keep working.
check: How well your heart and lungs work during long activity is...
How long a muscle can keep working is...
How many parts of health-related fitness?
lessons.try: Do one activity for each part: jog, push-ups, wall sit, stretch.

learn: Flexibility is how far your joints can move.
Static stretches are held for 15 to 30 seconds after exercise.
Never bounce in a stretch, and stretch only until you feel a gentle pull.
lessons.try: Do a sit-and-reach stretch and measure how far you reach.

learn: A SMART goal is Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound.
"I will do 15 push-ups by the end of the month" is a SMART goal.
Track progress in a log.
check: What does the M in SMART stand for?
lessons.try: Write a SMART fitness goal and start a log.

learn: Your heart pumps blood through blood vessels to every part of your body.
Blood carries oxygen and nutrients to muscles.
A child's resting heart rate is about 70 to 100 beats per minute.
check: What does blood carry to muscles?
A child's resting heart rate is about...
lessons.try: Count your resting pulse for 30 seconds and double it.

learn: Your lungs breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide.
Exercise makes you breathe faster to get more oxygen to your muscles.
Regular exercise strengthens breathing muscles.
check: Why do you breathe faster in exercise?
lessons.try: Count breaths per minute at rest and after one minute of running in place.

learn: Muscles pull on bones to move your body.
Muscles work in pairs: when your biceps contract, your triceps relax.
Weight-bearing exercise like jumping makes bones stronger.
lessons.try: Bend your arm and feel your biceps contract.

learn: Dribble with the inside and outside of your foot using small touches.
Keep the ball close and your head up to see the field.
Change speed and direction to get past defenders.
lessons.try: Dribble through a line of cones without touching them.

learn: Pass with the inside of your foot for accuracy.
Plant your non-kicking foot beside the ball, pointing at the target.
Trap (stop) a ball by cushioning it with the inside of your foot.
check: Which part of the foot is best for accurate passes?
lessons.try: Pass back and forth with a partner 20 times.

learn: For a powerful shot, kick with your laces (the top of your foot).
Keep your knee over the ball to keep it low.
Aim for the corners of the goal.
check: Knee over the ball keeps the shot...
lessons.try: Shoot at a target from ten steps away.

learn: Striking means hitting an object with a body part or an implement.
A volleyball underhand serve uses a flat hand and a swing from low to high.
Step forward with the opposite foot.
lessons.try: Serve a balloon or soft ball underhand to a partner.

learn: Hold a paddle with a "handshake" grip.
Keep your eye on the ball and swing level.
Return to ready position after each hit.
lessons.try: Bounce a ball on a paddle ten times.

learn: A volley means hitting the ball before it touches the ground.
In volleyball, the forearm pass (bump) uses flat forearms together.
Bend your knees and lift with your legs, not your arms.
check: A volley is hitting the ball...
lessons.try: Bump a balloon to keep it in the air as long as you can.

learn: Good teammates communicate, encourage and share the ball.
Everyone has a role, and every role matters.
Celebrate team success, not just your own.
check: Does every role on a team matter?
lessons.try: Play a team game and say one encouraging thing to each teammate.

learn: Fair play means following rules and respecting opponents and officials.
Accept a referee's call even if you disagree.
Never cheat, even if no one is watching.
check: If you disagree with the referee, you...
Should you cheat if no one is watching?
lessons.try: Make a fair play pledge with your family.

learn: Win with humility: don't brag.
Lose with grace: congratulate the other team.
Both winning and losing teach lessons.
lessons.try: After a game, name one thing you did well and one to improve.

learn: MyPlate shows a healthy meal: half fruits and vegetables, a quarter grains and a quarter protein, with dairy on the side.
Make at least half your grains whole grains, like whole wheat bread or brown rice.
Eat a rainbow of vegetables for different vitamins.
check: How much of MyPlate is fruits and vegetables?
Why eat a rainbow of vegetables?
lessons.try: Draw your dinner on a MyPlate diagram.

learn: Carbohydrates give energy. Proteins build and repair muscles.
Healthy fats, like those in nuts and fish, help your brain.
Vitamins and minerals keep your body working; calcium builds bones.
lessons.try: Find a food for each nutrient in your kitchen.

learn: Too much added sugar can harm teeth and health.
Soda and many juices have lots of sugar. Water and milk are better choices.
Read labels to compare sugar.
lessons.try: Compare the sugar in a soda and a glass of milk with a grown-up.

learn: Germs are bacteria and viruses too small to see.
They spread through coughs, sneezes, touching surfaces and sharing cups.
Good hygiene breaks the chain of spreading germs.
lessons.try: Put glitter on your hands and shake hands. See how "germs" spread.

learn: Shower or bathe regularly, especially after sweating.
Wear clean clothes and use deodorant as you get older.
Keep nails trimmed and hair clean.
check: When is a shower especially important?
lessons.try: Make a weekly hygiene checklist.

learn: Stay home when sick so you don't spread germs.
Rest, drink fluids and follow a doctor's advice.
Vaccines help protect people from some serious diseases.
check: What helps protect people from some serious diseases?
lessons.try: Make a "feel better" plan for when you're sick.

learn: Smoke alarms warn of fire. They should be tested monthly.
Have two ways out of every room and a family meeting place.
If there's smoke, stay low and crawl to an exit. Never hide.
check: How often should smoke alarms be tested?
How many ways out should each room have?
lessons.try: Draw a fire escape plan for your home.

learn: Swim with a buddy and a grown-up watching.
Use sunscreen with SPF 30 or more and reapply every two hours.
During lightning, go indoors. "When thunder roars, go indoors."
check: A buddy and a grown-up watching
lessons.try: Make a summer safety poster.

learn: Many household products, like cleaners, are poisonous.
Only take medicine from a trusted adult.
The Poison Help line in the U.S. is 1-800-222-1222.
check: The U.S. Poison Help line number is...
lessons.try: With a grown-up, check that cleaners are stored safely.

learn: Stress is how your body and mind react to challenges.
A little stress can help you focus, like before a test. Too much can make you feel sick or worried.
Signs of stress include headaches, trouble sleeping and feeling grumpy.
check: Which is a sign of stress?
lessons.try: List three things that cause you stress.

learn: Healthy ways to cope include exercise, deep breathing, talking to someone and getting enough sleep.
Box breathing: breathe in for 4, hold for 4, out for 4, hold for 4.
Breaking a big task into small steps reduces stress.
check: Which is a healthy coping strategy?
In box breathing, you breathe in for...
Breaking a task into small steps...
lessons.try: Practise box breathing for one minute.

learn: It's brave to ask for help.
Trusted adults include parents, teachers, school counsellors and coaches.
If someone ever talks about hurting themselves, tell a trusted adult right away.
check: If someone talks about hurting themselves, you...
Tell a trusted adult right away
lessons.try: Make a list of trusted adults you can talk to.

learn: Healthy friends respect each other, share and listen.
Friends can disagree and still be friends.
A good friend doesn't pressure you to do things you know are wrong.
check: Can friends disagree and stay friends?
Doesn't pressure you to do wrong
lessons.try: Write three qualities of a good friend.

learn: Bullying is when someone repeatedly hurts, scares or leaves out another person on purpose.
It can be physical (hitting), verbal (name-calling), social (leaving out) or online (cyberbullying).
Bullying is never the target's fault.
lessons.try: Talk with a grown-up about the four kinds of bullying.

learn: A bystander sees bullying and does nothing. An upstander helps.
Upstanders can tell the bully to stop, help the target walk away, or tell an adult.
Being kind to the target afterward helps a lot.
lessons.try: Role-play being an upstander with a family member.
